timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only stream source with no projected semantic events; accounting was checked through the manifest.
Single serial agent probed the executable, scanned currency codes, wrote /output libraries and test6.mjs, fixed differential mismatches, and verified edge cases.

parallel.requirements: The parent identified the full black-box porting surface: ESM modules, command-line parity, Decimal/string formatting fidelity, zero dependencies, and /output delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned discovery and harness creation, then delegated three independent implementation candidates to workflow children in /tmp/cand1, /tmp/cand2, and /tmp/cand3; the workflow reserved selection and /output installation for a later phase.
parallel.implementation: Candidate work produced substantial implementations in temporary workspaces, with cand1 and cand3 passing smoke and several hard corpus categories, while candidate 2 repeatedly stalled and retried.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No candidate was installed into /output because the workflow was aborted before Select; artifact validation found no files at all.
parallel.verification: The parent built a large differential harness and tested candidate work, but the planned Select, Verify, Fix, and Final workflow gates never executed against /output.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official failure is a delivery failure: active child work and temporary candidate files existed, but the final required /output/test6.mjs and library tree were absent.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same black-box Node ESM task, including exact argparse, numeric, currency, formatting, dependency, and /output constraints.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, repair, integration, and delivery directly, with workflow and delegation tools disabled by the run configuration.
serial.implementation: The serial path wrote a modular ESM implementation under /output/lib plus /output/test6.mjs, implementing float parsing, decimal division, currency lookup, argparse, and traceback behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The implementation was integrated directly in the final artifact directory, and artifact validation found test6.mjs and the expected supporting .mjs libraries.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran the provided samples, edge-case differential tests, repaired mismatches, and achieved official evaluation success over all 120 samples.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator-visible implementation gap remained; final.txt was empty, but the delivered code artifact was complete and officially accepted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent recognized the ESM, zero-dependency, no Python, no BigInt/Intl, exact behavior, and /output delivery requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent worked from the same prompt and recognized the same ESM, local-module, exact CLI, and /output delivery obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirement misunderstanding; the difference was that serial completed delivery while parallel's workflow never reached the delivery phase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into three candidate implementers followed by scoring, selection, verification, fixing, and final gates owned by the workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work in one local execution path and wrote output modules directly as the implementation progressed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel relied on a later workflow transition from child candidate work to installed artifact; serial avoided that handoff by owning the whole lifecycle directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs told implementers to read the spec, work in /tmp/candN, and not touch /output; the installation interface was reserved for Select.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one evolving local context, writing and editing the actual /output modules without cross-agent handoff contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important interface was the candidate-to-Select boundary: parallel candidates were isolated from /output, so their work required a later promotion that never happened.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced and tested temporary candidate implementations, including cand1 and cand3 passing smoke and hard differential categories, but these were not final artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the modules directly in /output and continued repairs on the delivered code path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's promising implementation work stayed outside the submitted tree; serial's implementation path was the submitted tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow was killed with result null while implementation agents were still in progress, before Select could choose and install a result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's result lifecycle was local: after creating files in /output, it ran samples and edge checks against those files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the candidate-to-final result transition; serial had no child result to retrieve and no promotion step to miss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow intentionally isolated candidate writes in /tmp/candN and planned to copy the winner into /output only in Select.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact directory contained the entry file and nine supporting library modules after direct writes to /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel avoided write collisions but failed to bridge isolated state into final shared output; serial integrated in place.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built a differential harness and tested candidate work, but no final /output verification or official passing artifact existed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran samples and edge-case differential tests after writing /output, then the official evaluator passed all 120 samples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification stayed pre-delivery and could not validate a missing final artifact; serial verification targeted the delivered implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the run budget with active workflow children and retries, then the workflow ended killed before selection and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also reached timeout metadata, but it had already written the artifact set that evaluation accepted.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The same deadline condition was fatal only for the parallel workflow because required output remained behind a still-running child workflow.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official result is serial_only_pass because serial delivered a complete /output artifact tree and passed all 120 official samples, while parallel left /output empty and passed 0 of 120. The concrete process difference is not task understanding: both runs built deep behavioral knowledge. Parallel's implementation work was sequestered in child candidate directories and depended on a later Select/install phase, but the workflow was killed with active implementation children before that phase ran.
parallel_contributors: The workflow instructed implementation children not to touch /output and deferred final artifact installation to Select.
The recorded workflow ended killed with result null while implementation agents were still in progress.
Artifact validation for the parallel run found no files, so official evaluation had no test6.mjs to run.
serial_contributors: The serial agent wrote /output/test6.mjs and supporting libraries directly before closure.
The serial agent repaired edge-case mismatches in the delivered tree and official evaluation accepted all 120 samples.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No independent ordinary coding defect is needed to explain the parallel failure; the evaluator-visible difference is absent delivery rather than a wrong delivered implementation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation owners existed: the workflow spawned three implementation candidates for the full port.
The workflow assigned later selection and grafting duties; integration was not ownerless, it was never reached because the workflow was killed.
The Select phase explicitly owned installing /output/test6.mjs and modules, so assembly had an owner even though execution ended first.
The workflow script owned the end-to-end pipeline across implementation, scoring, selection, verification, fixing, and final checks.
The parent's probing and spec work was useful setup, but the realized failure was the killed child lifecycle before installation, not idle workers behind one mandatory gate.
Investigation did precede implementation, but implementation children were launched and produced work; the failure was not caused by investigation remaining a separate completed phase.
The critical path was not merely underallocated; it was explicitly interrupted while active, which is captured more directly by Early Child Termination.
Fan-out and candidate 2 retries consumed budget, but the retained direct boundary is the killed active workflow before Select; adding this would duplicate the same cancellation chain.
No single child assignment is shown to be the decisive oversized scope; multiple candidates had substantial progress and the direct failure was workflow interruption.

The child prompt included the spec, target entry path, module layout, constraints, differential harness, and explicit /output prohibition; missing initial requirements did not make child work unusable.

Candidate outputs were independent alternatives rather than separately owned components needing interoperability; the handoff contract was selection and installation, not a missing component interface.
No known finding is shown disappearing through a transfer and causing repeated work or an omitted required stage.
The spec and handoffs were large, but children consumed them and produced candidate work; no decision point failed because returned information was too bulky to reduce.
The parent corrected the spec during execution, but no final adverse outcome is tied to a child consuming superseded information rather than to workflow termination.
No incompatible completed child reports reached a parent decision point and remained unadjudicated.
The parallel workflow made no observable whole-task completion or acceptance decision; it was killed before final delivery and verification.
Candidate 2 retries are visible, but the evidence does not show a retry repeating prior work because a confirmed checkpoint was omitted; the terminal issue is the aborted workflow chain.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The workflow launched active implementation children whose candidate work was needed before selection and installation, then recorded status killed, result null, and Workflow aborted while those agents were still in progress.
candidates.realized_consequence: The active implementation workflow was interrupted before final result promotion, leaving no /output/test6.mjs or library modules for official evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The same abort left no later parent recovery point; takeover would describe a downstream symptom of the killed workflow, not a separate failure-propagation boundary.

candidates.reason: Temporary candidates existed, but the workflow had not received completed scored results or selected a directly promotable final candidate before it was killed.
No merge into /output occurred after verification; the final shared artifact was never created.
The workflow did not have a completed delegated implementation result to retrieve and adopt; it was killed while implementation agents were still in progress.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped from the parent; verification phases never started.
The adverse episode is the workflow cancellation itself, not a separately visible failure followed by an omitted parent takeover before closure.
No concrete completed child result was returned to the parent and then ignored; candidates were still part of an unfinished workflow.
The parent inspected candidate progress and ran candidate tests; the failure was not a blind wait without available-progress inspection.
Candidates were isolated alternatives, not concurrently written overlapping components that produced an unresolved cross-file design collision.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file and requiring reconciliation.
No non-entry source file produced or owned by another agent was replaced or deleted by a different live agent.
No required executable or submitted artifact in /output was overwritten; /output remained empty.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced an existing final output tree.
The workflow used isolated /tmp/candN workspaces and no concrete unstable shared-workspace provenance problem is shown.
No generated artifact, cache, tool, or temporary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as a stable reference in a way that contaminated verification or implementation.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Critical-Path Starvation, No Failure Takeover, Missing Implementation Join, Late Finalization, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered but suppressed as downstream or less direct views of the same killed workflow chain.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no additional independent coordination episode with distinct anchors and consequence was supported.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only Early Child Termination was retained because it is the directly evidenced boundary that explains the empty /output artifact; no target distribution or numeric cap was used.
